title: Site comparison preserves compact-support composition with a proper factor
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:U\to V$ and $f:V\to W$ be separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and suppose at least one of $h,f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Choose compactifications of $h,f,fh$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $F_u^e=Ru^e_!$ for their small-etale compact-support functors [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $F_u^p=Ru^p_!$ for their small-pro-etale functors on bounded-below etale-origin objects [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. Use their canonical compactification composition maps $\alpha^s_{f,h}:F_f^s F_h^s\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{fh}^s$ ($s=e,p$), obtained by proper/open interchange and ordinary direct-image composition [lem-sf-unbounded-compact-support-proper-composition, thm-sf-comp-composition]. For proper factors their identification with ordinary direct image is the one from the identity-open compactification [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For $u=tv$ with open $v$ and proper $t$, let
$$c_{u,M}=Rt_{p,*}(e_{v,M})\circ b_{t,v_{e,!}M}:C F_u^eM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_u^p C M,$$
where $b$ is the specified counit-mate direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and $e$ is the canonical open-extension comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. For every $L\in D^+(U_e,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] the named maps satisfy
$$c_{fh,L}\circ C_W(\alpha^e_{f,h,L})=\alpha^p_{f,h,C_UL}\circ F_f^p(c_{h,L})\circ c_{f,F_h^eL}.$$
The same equality holds after any canonical refinement comparison; on a proper map $u$ its $c_u$ is $b_u$ under the identity-open identifications.
